summary: SIEM feed s088_single is degraded due to genuine packet loss: 3.0% of TCP packets (87/2949) show missing data. Slicing was ruled out as cause. All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLAN, one-way, oversize, tool overload, truncation, tunnel) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream capture/forwarding loss, not slicing artifact. Frames were validated via IP header length so slicing is ruled out. 2.95% loss exceeds 1% threshold, consistent with SPAN/mirror buffer overflow or packet broker egress congestion dropping packets before they reach the SIEM's 1G port.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM will have gaps in flow and event correlation - missing TCP segments cause incomplete sessions, missed alerts and incomplete forensic timeline even though SIEM does not require full payload or bidirectional traffic.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN/mirror ports have small buffers and drop under bursts with no backpressure. Replacing SPAN with passive TAP plus broker aggregation provides lossless capture and eliminates the 3% gaps. If TAP already in use, add load-balancing or filtering at the broker to relieve egress congestion toward the 1G SIEM port.
